tickets.title: Review mortgage liquidity source analysis
tickets.text: Compare bank cash, short-term bond holdings, taxable brokerage sales, and vested employer shares as funding sources for the remaining down payment on the Portland townhouse, while preserving at least $80,000 in post-closing emergency reserves. Use Julian Nettlewhisk’s stated cash reserves of $172,000 and the $945,000 purchase price with $25,000 earnest money already paid.
tickets.evidence: Julian asked for a mortgage liquidity source analysis comparing bank cash, short-term bond holdings, taxable brokerage sales, and vested employer shares to fund the remaining down payment while preserving the stated reserve target; the agreed follow-up is due 2025-10-08.

tickets.title: Obtain underwriting asset documentation for earnest money source
tickets.text: Upload the most recent Teacup Comet Bank and Velvet Acorn Custody brokerage statements to the lender’s portal and document the source of the $25,000 earnest money withdrawal from Teacup Comet Bank checking.
tickets.evidence: the lender’s portal shows the most recent Teacup Comet Bank statement and Velvet Acorn Custody brokerage statement have not been uploaded, and the underwriter is asking for documentation tying the earnest money withdrawal to the source account; this remains needed by 2025-10-06.

tickets.title: Review cash-flow effect of rate-lock alternatives
tickets.text: Review the cash-flow effect of the updated loan terms’ rate-lock choices and financing contingency timeline before Julian responds to the lender.
tickets.evidence: The mortgage contact sent updated loan terms with a rate-lock choice and financing contingency timeline, and Julian wants the cash-flow effect of the lock alternatives reviewed before he responds; the agreed review is due 2025-10-10.

tickets.title: Resolve student loan payment discrepancy for underwriting
tickets.text: Reconcile the difference between the mortgage application’s $640 monthly student loan payment for Iris and the $410 income-driven payment shown on the current servicer statement. Update the underwriting debt-to-income calculation accordingly.
tickets.evidence: the mortgage application lists Iris’s student loan payment as $640 per month, while the current servicer statement provided by Iris shows a $410 income-driven payment, creating a different debt-to-income calculation for underwriting; resolution remains needed by 2025-10-07.

tickets.title: Update brokerage aggregation feed for current liquidity positions
tickets.text: Refresh the Velvet Acorn Custody aggregation feed in the planning portal to reflect current joint brokerage balances, including short-term bond positions and cash available for closing.
tickets.evidence: The Velvet Acorn Custody aggregation feed in the planning portal is showing a stale joint brokerage balance, so the liquidity worksheet is not reflecting the current cash and short-term bond positions available for closing; the agreed follow-up is due 2025-10-06.

tickets.title: Coordinate new-home insurance and liability review
tickets.text: Update the household’s insurance coverage from the current renters policy to include the new Portland townhouse purchase, reviewing property and liability exposure for Julian and Iris Nettlewhisk.
tickets.evidence: The townhouse purchase changes the household’s property and liability exposure, and the couple has only renters coverage in place through their current policy set;

tickets.title: Review tax-lot suitability for down-payment funding
tickets.text: Review the taxable ETF positions in the Velvet Acorn Custody brokerage account, identifying short-term gain lots and lower-gain long-term lots, to determine the most suitable holdings if brokerage assets are used for closing cash.
tickets.evidence: Lena noted that several taxable ETF positions have both short-term gain lots and lower-gain long-term lots, affecting which holdings may be most suitable if brokerage assets are used for closing cash; the agreed tax-lot review is due 2025-10-09.
